title: Bangla Awas Yojana List 2026: Check Name, Banglar Bari
meta_description: Check your name in the Bangla Awas Yojana (Banglar Bari) list 2026 district wise. Rs 1.2 lakh help, eligibility, payment status and how to verify online.

hero.one_liner: How to check if your name is in the West Bengal Bangla Awas Yojana (Banglar Bari) housing list, what the three list types mean, and what to do if you qualify but are missing.

what_is_it: Bangla Awas Yojana is the West Bengal rural housing scheme that helps poor families build a pucca house. In current district records it is published as Banglar Bari (Gramin), and both names point to the same beneficiary list.
It gives financial help to families living in a kutcha house or with no house of their own, so they can build a permanent home. The house is meant to include a kitchen space and a linked toilet.

The scheme is run by the Department of Panchayat and Rural Development, Government of West Bengal. Selection is based on survey data, not a fresh open application, which is why checking the list matters more than applying.
Most readers reach this page for one reason: to find out whether their name is on the list. The sections below cover exactly how to check, district wise, and what to do if your name is missing.
Knowing the exact name and the right portal saves wasted trips. Many families search the wrong website and conclude they were rejected when they simply looked in the wrong place.

This guide sticks to what is verified and points you to the official district sources, so you can check your status with confidence rather than relying on rumours from neighbours, and without relying on rumours from neighbours or agents.

extra_sections.heading: Bangla Awas Yojana and Banglar Bari: Same Scheme
content: People search for this scheme under several names, and it causes a lot of confusion. Bangla Awas Yojana, Banglar Bari and the West Bengal rural housing list all refer to the same programme.

West Bengal runs its rural housing under the Banglar Bari (Gramin) banner, and district administrations publish their provisional lists under that name. If you applied as Bangla Awas Yojana, you check the Banglar Bari list.

Because it is a state-run rural housing scheme, the live beneficiary lists are published on West Bengal district government websites, not on a single national page. That is the key thing to know before you start checking.
So treat the two names as one. The page below uses Bangla Awas Yojana and Banglar Bari interchangeably, because on the ground they are the same list.
If a neighbour found their name but you did not, it is often because the lists are split by block and panchayat. Make sure you opened the PDF for your own area, not a nearby one.

extra_sections.heading: How to Check the Bangla Awas Yojana List 2026
content: The most reliable way to check your name is on your own district's government website. Lists are published block wise and Gram Panchayat wise as PDF files.
Open your district site, which follows the pattern districtname.gov.in or districtname.nic.in. Look under the Notices or Announcements section for Banglar Bari rural housing.
Find your Block and Gram Panchayat, then open the Provisional list. You will usually see three separate lists: Eligible, Ineligible, and Inactive.
Search the Eligible list for your name and application or registration number. If your name is there, your house assistance is approved subject to the next verification stages.
Keep your application or registration number ready before you start. It makes finding your row in a long PDF far quicker than scanning by name alone.
If you cannot find your district site, search the district name with the words rural housing notice. The official .gov.in or .nic.in result is the one to trust.

extra_sections.heading: Step by Step: Finding Your Name

steps.title: Open your district government website
steps.description: Go to your district site, such as coochbehar.gov.in or hooghly.nic.in. These publish the official Banglar Bari (Gramin) provisional lists.

steps.title: Find Notices or Announcements
steps.description: Look in the Notices or Announcements menu for a Banglar Bari or Rural Housing entry. District sites post the provisional lists here as PDFs.

steps.title: Select your Block and Gram Panchayat
steps.description: Lists are organised block wise and GP wise. Open the PDF for your own block and panchayat to keep the search manageable.

steps.title: Check the Eligible, Ineligible and Inactive lists
steps.description: Search for your name and application number in each. Eligible means approved, Inactive means approved but payment is blocked, Ineligible means rejected at verification.

steps.title: Cross-check on the PMAY-G portal
steps.description: You can also search the national record at pmayg.nic.in under Stakeholders, then IAY/PMAYG Beneficiary, using Advanced Search for West Bengal.

extra_sections.heading: What the three list types mean
extra_sections.content:
Eligible means your name is approved by the Gram Sabha and your house assistance is cleared for the next stages.

Inactive means you are approved but payment is held up, usually because Aadhaar is not linked to your bank account, the account is dormant, or the IFSC changed after a bank merger.

Ineligible means you were screened out at verification, often for owning a pucca house or for a data mismatch. You can dispute this with proof.

extra_sections.heading: How Much You Get and How Payment Reaches You
content: The total assistance is Rs 1.2 lakh in plains areas and Rs 1.3 lakh in hill or difficult areas. It is paid in installments tied to your construction progress, not as a single lump sum.
The first installment is Rs 60,000, released to your Aadhaar-linked bank account by direct transfer once your name is approved and entered in the system.

The remaining amount is released in further installments as your house reaches set construction stages, such as lintel level and completion. The exact split follows your latest district or state housing notice.
At each stage a local officer verifies progress, often with a geo-tagged photo of your house, before the next installment is cleared. Eligible families may also get MGNREGA wages for the labour.
Treat the money as a construction grant, not free cash. Each installment is tied to you actually building to a defined stage, and the field check must pass before the next one is released.
Make sure the bank account is active and Aadhaar-seeded before the first installment is due. A dormant or unseeded account is the top reason an approved name slips into the Inactive list.

extra_sections.heading: Why your name may be missing
extra_sections.content:
The base survey data for this scheme is old, so families missed in the original survey, or who became poor or homeless later, often do not appear. This is the single most common reason a genuine family is not on the list.

The Awaas Plus survey was meant to capture these missed households, but it has not reached every block evenly. If you truly qualify and have no pucca house, this is fixable through a grievance, not a reason to give up.

extra_sections.heading: What to Do If Your Name Is Missing or Wrongly Listed
content: If you are not on the Eligible list but believe you qualify, start at your Gram Panchayat. Carry your Aadhaar, ration card and anything that shows your housing condition.
Ask whether the Awaas Plus survey has covered your household. If it has not, request in writing that your family be surveyed and added.
For a formal complaint, use the grievance section on pmayg.nic.in, giving your State, District and Block. Keep a copy of the complaint and any acknowledgement number.

If you are on the Ineligible list and disagree, take documents proving your case to the Block Development Office. Wrongful exclusions, like being wrongly coded as owning a pucca house, can be corrected.
Be persistent but patient. Grievances and Awaas Plus additions take time, so keep copies of every application and follow up at the Gram Panchayat rather than waiting silently.
If your name is on the Ineligible list purely due to a data error, the Block Development Office can correct it. Carry originals, since a clear document usually settles a wrong code quickly.
Keep your grievance reference number safe. It is what lets you follow up and prove you raised the issue if the matter drags on.

extra_sections.text: Not finding your name does not always mean you are ineligible. Survey errors and households missed between surveys are common, and a grievance with proof is the correct path if you genuinely qualify.

how_to_apply.title: Understand there is no open application
how_to_apply.description: You cannot simply apply online. Beneficiaries are picked from survey data and approved by the Gram Sabha, so the first task is checking the list, not filling a form.

how_to_apply.title: Confirm your survey status at the GP
how_to_apply.description: Visit your Gram Panchayat and ask whether your household is in the SECC or Awaas Plus survey data. If not, request inclusion in the next survey.

how_to_apply.title: Keep Aadhaar and bank ready
how_to_apply.description: Make sure your Aadhaar is linked to an active bank account, since all installments are paid by direct transfer to that account.

how_to_apply.title: Track the provisional list
how_to_apply.description: Watch your district government website for new provisional Banglar Bari lists, and check the Eligible list when each batch is published.

faqs.question: How to check bangla awas yojana list 2026 online?
faqs.answer:
Open your district government website, such as coochbehar.gov.in or hooghly.nic.in, and look under Notices or Announcements for the Banglar Bari rural housing list.

Find your Block and Gram Panchayat, then open the Provisional list and search the Eligible list for your name. You can also check the national record at pmayg.nic.in.

faqs.question: What is the difference between bangla awas yojana and banglar bari?
faqs.answer:
They refer to the same West Bengal rural housing scheme and the same list. Bangla Awas Yojana is the common search name, and Banglar Bari (Gramin) is the name used in current district records.

If you applied as Bangla Awas Yojana, you check the Banglar Bari list on your district site.

faqs.question: How much money is given under bangla awas yojana?
faqs.answer:
The total is Rs 1.2 lakh in plains areas and Rs 1.3 lakh in hill or difficult areas. It is paid in installments tied to construction stages, not as one payment.

The first installment is Rs 60,000, released to your Aadhaar-linked bank account after your name is approved.

faqs.question: What is the bangla awas yojana new list?
faqs.answer:
The new list is the latest provisional batch of beneficiaries that district administrations publish, block wise and GP wise, after survey and Gram Sabha verification.

Each district releases its own dated notice, so check your district government website for the most recent one.

faqs.question: What does Inactive mean on the beneficiary list?
faqs.answer:
Inactive means your name is approved but your payment is blocked. The usual reasons are Aadhaar not linked to your bank account, a dormant account, or an IFSC change after a bank merger.

Fix the bank or Aadhaar issue through your Gram Panchayat, and the payment can be released.

faqs.question: Why is my name not on the bangla awas yojana list?
faqs.answer:
Most missing names are families not captured in the base survey data, which is several years old, or who became homeless or poor afterwards.

If you genuinely qualify with no pucca house, ask your Gram Panchayat about the Awaas Plus survey and file a grievance with proof.

faqs.question: Can I apply for bangla awas yojana if my name is not listed?
faqs.answer:
There is no open online application to add yourself to the list. Beneficiaries are selected from survey data.

You can request that your household be included in the Awaas Plus survey through your Gram Panchayat, which is the route for missed families.

faqs.question: How many installments are given under the scheme?
faqs.answer:
The assistance is released in installments linked to construction progress. The first is Rs 60,000 after approval.

The balance is paid as the house reaches set stages like lintel level and completion. The exact split follows your latest district or state notice.

faqs.question: What documents do I need for bangla awas yojana?
faqs.answer:
You mainly need an Aadhaar card linked to your bank account, a bank passbook, and a MGNREGA Job Card for construction wages.

Keep land proof handy if you own the plot. The Gram Panchayat handles most of the paperwork once you are on the Eligible list.

faqs.question: Is there an income limit for eligibility?
faqs.answer:
There is no single fixed income cut-off. Selection uses survey deprivation markers, like having no pucca house, no working adult, or being a female-headed or SC/ST household.

Owning a pucca house, a large landholding, or certain vehicles makes a family ineligible.
